_notes: One entry per agent tool. 'command' is appended to the codegraph binary (no shell is used).
Args with 'positional': true are passed as plain arguments, others use their 'flag'.
Args with 'path': true are confined to the repo root by the wrapper.
'json': true appends --json. 'root_flag': true appends --root . (the wrapper runs with cwd = repo root).
Entries with a 'verify' field use commands or flags that the agent-workflows doc does not fully specify. Check them with `codegraph help advanced` before relying on them.

tools.name: repo_orient
tools.description: Compact map of the repo: summary, ranked focus targets, bounded tree, health counts, omitted counts, next commands. Always the first call on a repo. Use budget 'small' first; 'medium' only if small is not enough. Scope to a subdirectory with 'paths'.

args.name: budget
args.description: Packet size. Default small.

args.name: paths
args.description: Optional subdirectory to scope the map, relative to the repo root.

tools.name: packet_get
tools.description: Compact orientation packet for one file (symbols, role, links). Use on the top focus targets from repo_orient.

args.name: file
args.description: File path relative to the repo root.

args.name: max_symbols
args.description: Cap on symbols returned, e.g. 25.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Find targets when you have a query but no file or handle. Returns ranked anchors with stable handles, evidence, neighbors and follow-ups. Mode 'symbol' for symbol-like terms, 'text' when docs or prose should rank higher, 'graph' with from_file for neighbors of a file, 'sql' for SQL objects. Default is hybrid, code-first.

args.name: query
args.description: Words or concepts, e.g. 'validate user'.

args.name: mode
args.description: Omit for hybrid.

args.name: from_file
args.description: Start file for mode 'graph'.

args.name: depth
args.description: Hops for mode 'graph'. Keep at 1-2.

tools.name: find_symbol
tools.description: Which declaration has this identity? Deterministic lookup by name or 'path::Name'. Returns portable handles to pass to explain, refs and callers. Narrow large results with kind, exported or file_glob.

args.name: name
args.description: Symbol name or 'src/file.ts::Name'.

args.name: kind
args.description: e.g. function, class, interface.

args.name: exported
args.description: Only exported symbols.

args.name: file_glob
args.description: Project-relative glob, e.g. 'src/api/**'.

args.name: limit
args.description: Max results. Keep at or below 50.

tools.name: explain
tools.description: Bounded explanation packet for one target: dependencies, references, snippets, duplicate context, follow-ups. Accepts a handle from search or find_symbol, a file path, a symbol name or a SQL object name. Main drill-down tool.

args.name: target
args.description: Handle (preferred), file path or symbol name.

tools.name: refs
tools.description: Semantic references to a symbol. For a known symbol, use this or callers instead of explore. Accepts a handle, a search location or a unique exact name. May be incomplete for method calls in some languages.
tools.verify: Flags and --json support not confirmed in the doc.

args.name: target
args.description: Handle, location or unique exact name.

tools.name: callers
tools.description: Who calls this symbol. For a known symbol, start here or with refs. Caller lists can be a lower bound for method calls in some languages.
tools.verify: Flags and --json support not confirmed in the doc.

args.name: target
args.description: Handle or unique exact name.

tools.name: goto
tools.description: Jump to a definition. Accepts a handle or a location from search output.
tools.verify: Flags and --json support not confirmed in the doc.

args.name: target
args.description: Handle or location.

tools.name: deps
tools.description: What a file depends on (outgoing imports). Use for module-level dependency direction.
tools.verify: Depth/limit flags not confirmed for the CLI; the doc only shows them for the library wrapper.

args.name: file
args.description: File path relative to the repo root.

tools.name: rdeps
tools.description: What depends on a file (reverse dependencies). Use to see who consumes a module.
tools.verify: Depth/limit flags not confirmed for the CLI; the doc only shows them for the library wrapper.

args.name: file
args.description: File path relative to the repo root.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Current source of a file, paged. Use last, for the few nodes that decide the answer. Budgeted (about 5 calls per task). Secret-prone configs return keys only.

args.name: path
args.description: File path relative to the repo root.

args.name: offset
args.description: First line, 1-based.

args.name: limit
args.description: Number of lines. 100-200 is usually enough.

args.name: max_bytes
args.description: Output byte cap for the page.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Raw text or regex search. Use for log messages, config keys, string literals and anything that is not a symbol.
tools.verify: Flags not confirmed in the doc.

args.name: pattern
args.description: Text or regex. Must not start with '-'.

tools.name: explore
tools.description: One narrow question answered with context from the top hybrid-search results: anchors, packets, paths, reverse dependencies, candidate tests, follow-ups. Use sparingly. It does not plan subqueries or prove behavior. For a known symbol use refs or callers instead.

args.name: query
args.description: A narrow question, e.g. 'how does auth reach db?'.

args.name: no_source
args.description: Skip source packets to keep output small.

tools.name: doctor
tools.description: Diagnose package/runtime problems. Call once if codegraph fails with an install or runtime error. Do not use for normal exploration.

builtin_tools.name: use_skill
builtin_tools.description: Load the full playbook for a skill by name. Call this before starting a task covered by a skill.

args.name: name
args.description: Skill name from the available skills list.

builtin_tools.name: digest
builtin_tools.description: Summarize a large stored result (from a truncated tool output) into a short cited summary. Not for exact code, names or counts.

args.name: result_id
args.description: Id from a '[truncated ... r_xxxx]' note.

args.name: question
args.description: What you need to know from it.

args.name: max_tokens
args.description: Default 300.

builtin_tools.name: scratchpad
builtin_tools.description: Save or read working notes: repo root, key handles, conclusions. Use it so old tool output is not needed again.

args.name: action
args.description: set, get or list.

args.name: key
args.description: Required for set and get.

args.name: value
args.description: Required for set.

builtin_tools.name: find_files
builtin_tools.description: Read-only recursive, case-insensitive filename search. Use for requests to find files or folders by name or glob (for example '*harness*' or '*eval*'). Searches basenames under the repository or a confined subdirectory.

args.name: pattern
args.description: One or more comma-separated filename globs, e.g. '*harness*,*eval*'.

args.name: directory
args.description: Optional repo-relative directory to search. Defaults to the repo root.

args.name: limit
args.description: Maximum paths returned, capped at 100. Defaults to 50.

builtin_tools.name: run_shell
builtin_tools.description: Execute a shell command with the workspace as its working directory. Use this to perform requested workspace inspections and operations rather than telling the user to run the command. Commands can modify files and are not sandboxed to the workspace.

args.name: command
args.description: Shell command to execute. It runs in the workspace directory and is subject to the configured timeout, tool-call budget, and output cap.

builtin_tools.name: create_architecture_diagram
builtin_tools.description: Create a standalone HTML architecture diagram only when the user asks for an architecture diagram, architecture overview visualization, or architectural flow chart. Lazily invokes an architecture analyst subagent to inspect the requested repository scope using read-only tools, then a specialist HTML diagram writer. The completed HTML is delivered to VS Code and opened automatically.

args.name: question
args.description: The user's requested architecture diagram scope and details. Include the whole repository or the specifically requested subsystem/flow.
